THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge & Addl.MACT, Bhalki, in MVC No.6/2018 in terms of the judgment and award dated 06.05.2022.
2.

The claimant met with an accident on 03.07.2017, when he and another were riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-24/U-6046 which was dashed against by a Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 38/6704.
As a result of the accident, the claimant suffered crushed and degloved injury to the left foot.
The claimant was shifted to Government Hospital, Bhalki, where crime No.115/2017 was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 of IPC and Section 187 of M.V.Act.
The claimant was aged 35 years and was employed as peon in Datta Madhymika School Vijaynagar and was drawing a monthly salary of Rs.17,048/-.
The claimant, therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the lorry referred above.
3. The claim petition was opposed by the insurer who denied the accident as well as injury suffered by the claimant.
It also alleged that the rider of the offending vehicle had violated the terms of the policy and that he did not possess a driving licence.
It also denied the age, avocation and income of the claimant as well as the medical expenses incurred by him for his treatment.

4. The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P15 while doctor was examined as PW.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered locomotar disability to the extent of 40 to 45% to the limb.

5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal considered the income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.16,000/- per month and the disability suffered by him as 10% to the whole body and awarded the following compensation;
Sl.No. Heads of Compensation Amount in Rs. 1 Pain & Suffering 5,000/-

2. Medical Expenses 57,000/-
3. Conveyance, attendant 3,000/-
charges & nourishment 4. Loss of future earning 3,07,200/-

2 capacity on account of permanent disabilities 5. Amenities and unhappiness 3,000/-
 Total 3,73,200/-
 6.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the claimant has filed this appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the tribunal has committed an error in considering the notional income of the claimant at Rs.16,000/- per month, while the salary certificate at Ex.P13 disclosed the income of the claimant as Rs.17,048/- per month.
He submitted that the tribunal also committed an error in considering 10% as the disability.
He also submitted that the compensation awarded under the conventional heads is also very meager and calls for interference.
Learned counsel submitted that the tribunal while adding up the compensation had committed an arithmetical error and that the same may be corrected.
8. Learned counsel for the Insurer on the other hand, submitted that the claimant was employed in the school.
She submitted though claimant deposed before the tribunal that he lost income during his treatment for a period of 6 months, no material was placed in that record.
for which time he was taken treatment.

She submits that the claimant did not suffer any loss of earning capacity due to disability suffered by him and therefore the compensation was wrongly awarded by the tribunal towards loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.

She further submitted that the tribunal has assessed the compensation by treating the age of the claimant as 30 years, while the claimant himself claimed that his age was 35 years and the appropriate multiplier was 16 and not 18 which was applied by the tribunal.
She however did not dispute the fact that the tribunal committed an arithmetical error while adding up the compensation determined.
Therefore, submits that on all these accounts the judgment passed by the tribunal is erroneous and the appellant/claimant should not be further rewarded with enhanced compensation.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. If we add up the compensation determined by the tribunal, the total compensation works out to Rs.3,75,200/- as against Rs.3,73,200/- determined by the tribunal.

The tribunal had determined the compensation by considering the notional income of the claimant at Rs.16,000/- per month as against the monthly income of Rs.17,048/- and had treated the disability at 10% to the whole body and applied maximum multiplier of 18 while in the facts and circumstances of the case, the multiplier applicable was 16 having regard to the fact that the age of the claimant was 35 years.
The claimant did not produce any document to demonstrate that he was not paid any salary during the period of treatment or he was terminated from employment due to the disability suffered.
Yet the Tribunal awarded compensation towards loss of earning capacity due to the disability.

However, it is Dinkar S/O Kishanrao Gaikwad vs Prakash S/O Gurappa Tonne And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47721785/
3 unfortunate that the insurer had not challenged the quantum of compensation determined by the tribunal and has allowed it to remain.

sentences.text: It is noticed that the tribunal had awarded a meager compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.3,000/- towards conveyance, attendant charges & nourishment and Rs.3,000/- towards amenities and unhappiness.
Since the claimant was awarded more than just compensation, this Court considers it appropriate to enhance the compensation by a sum of Rs.4,000/-.
11. In that view of the matter, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation determined by the tribunal is enhanced to Rs.3,75,200/- to a sum of Rs.3,79,200/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.4,000/- shall carry interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization.
The insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation with interest before the Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
